tasks.short: Verify remote-sensing data integrity and accuracy

steps.what: Select data integrity checks and capture accuracy references and tolerances
Compare data integrity, metadata and numeric errors against selected validation limits
Verify accuracy in context, investigate discrepancies and accept or reject the dataset

tasks.design: Configure fixed integrity and numeric accuracy checks in the {OTHER} geospatial image-analysis system. The technician selects valid references and tolerances, investigates results and accepts or rejects each exact dataset version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated metadata and numeric comparisons can be mixed with scientific interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native geospatial validation tools can repeat specified comparisons without choosing scientific acceptance criteria.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise misregistration, poor references or artefacts that pass simple numeric tests.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the dataset is fit for the intended scientific use.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated comparison; scientific acceptance responsibility stays with the technician.

reach.learn: Choose independent references and understand error measures.

evidence.claim: Fixed geospatial integrity and numeric accuracy comparisons can be configured separately from scientific acceptance; savings are an unmeasured model-knowledge scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is data-quality verification, excluding original acquisition, image preparation and downstream data integration.

OTHER is geospatial image-analysis software. Dataset producers supply raster files, checksums, coordinate reference system, pixel size, acquisition time, band definitions and no-data encoding in their existing acquisition workflow before s1.

The technician records dataset version, expected metadata, reference identifiers and coordinates, units, test selection and tolerances during retained s1 time. Reference survey owners provide existing reference observations; no new field collection or free quality flag is assumed.
s2 produces test results from s1's specification. Missing metadata or unsuitable reference observations require manual investigation in s1 and s3 and receive no automatic-check saving.
Test native tools first. Existing validation runtime earns no saving; only current repeated human comparisons are changed. Additional focal upkeep is 8 hours per 100 baseline hours.
unknowns: Quality and independence of reference observations
research_questions: Which repeated manual comparisons can native checks reproduce without concealing spatial artefacts?

already_counted.description: Specification, field capture, investigation and acceptance remain human.

incremental.description: Maintain validation settings and investigate additional test failures.

approvals.approved_version: Exact dataset version, reference versions, validation specification and results bound to the quality decision in s3; any change voids acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+40=75; gross=25, focal upkeep=8, net=17. Conservative 3-9 allows incomplete metadata and spatial artefacts requiring manual work; scientific acceptance retains all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Integrate remote sensing and other geospatial datasets

steps.what: Specify how remotely sensed data should align with other geospatial data
Integrate datasets using the specified reprojection, resampling and join operations
Check spatial alignment and meaning and accept or correct the integrated dataset

tasks.design: Save the technician's checked transformation sequence as a native model in the {OTHER} geospatial analysis system. Repeat exact reprojection, resampling and joins for compatible inputs, then have the technician inspect spatial alignment and scientific meaning before accepting the result.
tasks.previous_blocker: Compatible datasets can require repeated manual setup and execution of the same transformations.
tasks.enabler_now: Native processing models can repeat the specified operations with a recorded parameter set.
tasks.still_hard: Choose appropriate resolution and join semantics and identify misleading spatial or temporal alignment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise that geometrically aligned datasets can still describe incompatible observations.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated operation setup; integration-method choices and acceptance stay human.

reach.learn: Understand resampling effects, temporal compatibility and join cardinality.

evidence.claim: Native geospatial processing models can repeat a specified integration sequence; method selection and the savings scenario remain model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is integration of existing datasets, excluding upstream quality verification, acquisition and downstream interpretation. Quality-check savings are not counted again here.

OTHER is geospatial analysis software. Dataset owners supply existing files, identifiers, versions, coordinate systems, pixel or geometry definitions, acquisition times, units and attribute dictionaries before s1.

The technician captures source versions, target coordinate system and extent, output resolution, resampling method, temporal match window, join keys, cardinality and no-data policy in retained s1 time. No free compatible-input flag is presumed.

s2 runs only the checked specification; missing metadata, new schemas or uncertain joins stop for manual handling. s3 verifies visual alignment and sample attribute meanings, not merely successful execution.
Test native processing models first. Already scripted runtime earns no saving; the scenario replaces currently repeated human setup. Additional focal upkeep is 8 hours per 100 baseline hours.
unknowns: Current use of native processing models
research_questions: Can native models reproduce accepted integrations without introducing duplicate joins or misleading resampling?

already_counted.description: Input specification, capture and scientific review remain.

incremental.description: Maintain processing parameters and handle schema changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact integrated dataset version, source versions, transformation parameters and integration log checked in s3; any change voids acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+25=60; gross=40, upkeep=8, central net=32. Conservative 6-18 assumes only recurring compatible inputs avoid manual setup; method choice and scientific review retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult specialists to determine project needs

steps.what: Consult scientists, surveyors, cartographers or engineers to determine project needs

tasks.design: Keep project-needs consultation with the technician and specialists. Existing project material in {DOCS} supports discussion without generating requirements or adding recording work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project needs must reconcile scientific purpose, constraints and stakeholder expectations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reference access supports consultation but does not replace it.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve ambiguous requirements and expose conflicts between desired accuracy, coverage and resources.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the question that reveals an unstated scientific or operational need.
tasks.altitude: Consultation duties and project authority stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Translate intended use into explicit coverage and quality needs.

evidence.claim: Determining project needs is a contextual specialist conversation, distinct from processing existing structured datasets.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's consultation contribution, excluding later detailed transformation specification, project approval and meeting-note production.
The project sponsor supplies the purpose before s1; specialists supply constraints and questions during discussion. No prior structured project-needs flag is assumed.

Specialists' existing participation remains unchanged outside the focal denominator. Native document access is sufficient; no new tool, capture duty or upkeep is added, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: Which specialist owns final project approval
research_questions: Which unstated requirements most often cause later rework?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No specialist discussion or requirements judgement is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adjust remotely sensed images for presentation

steps.what: Select image displays, image set categories and processing routines for presentation
Adjust remotely sensed images by applying the selected display and processing settings
Inspect presentation for misleading contrast, missing features and inappropriate categories before accepting it

tasks.design: Configure reusable display presets and batch rendering in the {OTHER} geospatial image-analysis system. The technician chooses the settings and checks the resulting presentation for meaningful visibility and misleading effects before accepting its exact version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applying the same approved display settings across images can require repeated manual setup.
tasks.enabler_now: Native presets can repeat specified processing while retaining the original image and parameters.
tasks.still_hard: Choose displays and categories that reveal relevant features without suggesting false distinctions.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the presentation is scientifically useful rather than merely attractive.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated display setup; presentation choices and acceptance remain human.

reach.learn: Explain how band selection and contrast affect interpretation.

evidence.claim: Copernicus supplies atmospherically corrected Sentinel-2 data and mosaics, supporting availability of prepared imagery rather than proving display-adjustment savings.
Reusable display presets can reduce repeated human setup; the proposed saving is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is presentation adjustment of already prepared images, excluding atmospheric correction, acquisition and data integration. Upstream preparation savings are not claimed here.

OTHER is geospatial image-analysis software. Existing image providers supply images and metadata before s1. The technician captures image versions, band assignments, stretch limits, units, no-data handling, category definitions and chosen routine parameters during retained s1 time.

s2 applies only s1's specified settings. Missing bands, changed units or unknown categories require manual adjustment with no repeat-setup saving. s3 examines actual feature visibility and interpretation, not just file creation.

Test native presets first. Existing rendering runtime is not human labour; the 30% baseline applies only to repeated manual setup and application that a preset actually removes. Additional focal upkeep is 7 hours per 100 baseline hours.
unknowns: Frequency of genuinely recurring display requirements
research_questions: Do presets reduce repeated setup while retaining scientifically useful feature visibility?

already_counted.description: Display choices, parameter capture and visual acceptance remain.

incremental.description: Maintain presets and investigate inconsistent renderings.

approvals.approved_version: Exact rendered image version, original image versions, display parameters and category definitions inspected in s3; any change voids acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=50+0+20=70; gross=30, upkeep=7, central net=23. Conservative 4-12 assumes many images require individual manual adjustment; setting selection and visual review retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician retains scientific choices and acceptance while native routines may reduce repeated comparisons, transformations and display setup.
reach: Translate scientific requirements into explicit quality and processing parameters.
role.ambitious_version: Use released repetitive-work time to investigate ambiguous image quality and integration issues with scientists.
